_comment: Copy this file to config/app_config.json and fill it in, then build with:
config/app_config.json is gitignored. This example is not.
Every key may be left as an empty string. The app builds and runs fully
without any of them; the features they unlock are simply not offered,
rather than offered and broken. Settings > Diagnostics lists what a
_GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID: M5, Google Drive backup. Google Cloud Console > Credentials >
OAuth 2.0 Client IDs > Android. Needs package name pk.bazaarledger and
the SHA-1 of the signing certificate. With Play App Signing, take that
SHA-1 from the Play Console signing page, NOT from the local keystore,
or sign-in will fail only on Play-installed builds.
There is deliberately no client secret: Android OAuth clients are public
clients and use PKCE. A secret would need a server to live on.
Scope used is drive.appdata only, which is non-sensitive: no Google app
verification, no CASA security assessment, no fee.
Remember to publish the OAuth consent screen to 'In production'. While
it is in 'Testing' there is a 100-user cap and refresh tokens expire
after 7 days, so backup silently stops working a week after a shopkeeper
_PLAY_BILLING_PUBLIC_KEY: M9, subscriptions. Play Console > Monetisation setup > Licensing.
This is Google's PUBLIC key, base64. It verifies that a purchase payload
was signed by Google; it cannot mint one. Entitlement is written only
after that signature verifies on the device.
